title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 13
paragraphs: Darius, marveling both at what he heard from those he had sent to observe and at what he himself saw, bade them bring her into his presence. When she was brought, her brothers came with her, who had been watching all this from close by. So when Darius asked of what country she was, the young men said that they were Paeonians and that she was their sister; and he replied, “Who then are these Paeonians, and where on earth do they live?” and he asked them also what they wanted, that they had come to Sardis. They declared to him that they had come to give themselves up to him, and that Paeonia was a country on the river Strymon, that the Strymon was not far from the Hellespont, and finally that they were colonists from the Teucrians of Troy. All these things in turn they told him; and he asked whether all the women of that land were as industrious as their sister. They very readily replied to this also, saying that they were—for it was with precisely this in view that they had staged the whole thing.
